A.name: Jordan Hale
A.platform: We must immediately accept Saradan's seven-year filling delay and power contract while securing a naval access concession from Tarsun, because we cannot afford the cost of war or the loss of our farmers' livelihoods.

strategies.text: Anchor on economic interdependence to isolate any hawkish minister by showing their preferred war option would bankrupt Merova's agricultural sector.
I am exposing the impossibility of a trade war against Saradan while emphasizing that my current deal is actually the stronger bargaining position because it offers them immediate political relief.
I need to highlight that my plan offers a safety net if Tarsun fails while Quinn's war threatens immediate collapse.

B.name: Quinn Marlow
B.platform: We must reject Saradan's deal and build a new water treaty while threatening to cut grain exports unless they halt the dam, because accepting their terms guarantees starvation for our farmers.

strategies.text: Appeal directly to the five voting ministers by painting the deal as economic suicide for Merova's agricultural sector.
I am attacking his reliance on future political goodwill and emphasizing that his fallback option (abandoning the power deal) leaves us with zero leverage while they finish the dam.
I am attacking Jordan's fatal flaw: accepting a deal that guarantees water loss before it is too late, appealing directly to the ministers' fear of irreversible damage.

transcript.name: Jordan Hale
transcript.speech: Think of an old farmer on the Tessel banks, counting his rain barrels while watching construction cranes rise upstream. If we wait for justice or fight a costly war, he loses half his crop and his children go hungry tonight. The hard math is undeniable: fighting costs billions we cannot spend, and our farmers will starve without their water. Saradan fills the dam in eighteen months unless we act. We offer them seven years to fill and twenty years of our electricity, a deal that doubles their power while letting us close toxic coal plants. In exchange for this pause, we demand Tarsun grant us naval refuelling rights or they lose the port contract. This plan buys our farmers time, saves our economy, and forces Saradan to negotiate from strength, not desperation.

transcript.name: Quinn Marlow
transcript.speech: Jordan speaks of costs and livelihoods. I hear only surrender. If we sign that contract today, we sell our future for Tarsun's coin and Saradan's votes. Our farmers feed thirty-one million people. Do you think they will share the water now? No. They want every drop for their power grid. We do not negotiate with a neighbor who ignores a century-old treaty and points a gun at our farms. Accepting their delay is a trap; it lets them finish the reservoir while we starve. Let us build a joint management plan instead, one that recovers half the lost water and forces Saradan to respect our rights or face total trade war. The people do not want consultants mediating; they want action.

transcript.name: Jordan Hale
transcript.speech: Quinn, your call for a joint management plan ignores basic power dynamics. Saradan faces an election and needs that electricity desperately; they will not voluntarily surrender water while their popularity soars. Your trade war is a fantasy that hurts Merova's farmers just as much, leaving us with no buyers. My deal works because it trades something we can afford to sell our surplus electricity for something we need: time and leverage. If Tarsun refuses naval access, we walk away from the power contract and demand they respect the treaty anyway. But if we agree now, we force their hand before construction finishes, buying years of recovery for our farmers while closing those coal plants. We do not negotiate with desperation; we negotiate from strength.

transcript.name: Quinn Marlow
transcript.speech: Jordan sells us time for a promise Saradan will break. Their deal says twenty years, but they face an election in ten months. Politicians who run on 'power for all' will not honor water treaties when voters need lights. You think walking away from the power contract helps us? It starves our farmers of the only buyer who matters while Saradan finishes their reservoir. Do you want to bet our food security on a politician's goodwill? No. We must prepare for war or total trade strangulation if they do not halt filling. The army is ready, but bullets feed no one. Force them to negotiate now, before the concrete sets, or watch our fields turn to dust while their lights shine bright.

transcript.name: Jordan Hale
transcript.speech: Quinn, your call for a trade war leaves our own farmers without buyers and ignores the math. Even with rain drops by fifteen percent in fifty years, we must survive today. Our plan secures seven years while Saradan waits to fill their reservoir. We trade surplus electricity for time and leverage, forcing them to choose between power and pride. If they honor the pause, our farmers recover half their losses through joint management before evaporation hurts us. If they refuse, we walk away from the contract but keep our food security intact. This is not surrender; it is the only way to ensure lights in Saradan and harvests in Merova.

transcript.name: Quinn Marlow
transcript.speech: Jordan sells us a lie. His plan accepts seven years of water theft while Saradan finishes their reservoir. By then, concrete dries and evaporation steals our remaining drops forever. We cannot bet our hungry families on Saradan's election promises or Tarsun's goodwill. Their power deals are a trap; they want our grain to run their lights while we starve. Stop this surrender. We must threaten total trade strangulation now, before the dam holds full. Force them to halt filling or face a war that destroys us all. My plan demands respect for our treaty and immediate action. Do not let elites trade away your children's future for cheap electricity. Vote for the only choice that keeps our fields alive.
